findings.summary: Making each PR head a parent of a records commit pulls all of main's history into the records ref, so the records history is no longer a separate root in practice.
findings.evidence: The request and Decision 1 describe refs/athena/records as 'a separate root, never merged into main'. A PR head descends from main, so after the first landing, git log of the records ref walks every code commit. A fetch of the ref transfers code objects, and a full-history secret scan of the ref re-scans code. Fix: State the consequence in the design. Tools that read records walk --first-parent only. The records tree stays separate even though ancestry does not. Say how the full-history secret scan avoids double work, and whether this weakens A4 lift-out or D72 stealth mode. Alternatively, compare it honestly against keep-refs listed in a records file.

findings.summary: The plan does not say who may write the checkpoint. A writer able to push a false checkpoint could make the incremental check skip unverified commits until the next full replay.
findings.evidence: The checkpoint holds the last passing main sha, the records sha and the verifier version. It is pushed to the same ref that writers update with fast-forward-only pushes. Only the weekly replay bounds a false checkpoint. Fix: Say which actor writes checkpoints (for example, only the check after a pass). Say that the check confirms the checkpointed main sha is an ancestor of the current main, and that a checkpoint the replay cannot reproduce turns main red.
findings.location: Decision 5 (checkpoint stored in the records branch)

findings.summary: 'Nothing unverified reaches main' rests on a host-required status, which is absent in D72 stealth mode and can be bypassed by an admin merge.
findings.evidence: Decision 2 enforces the guarantee at a 'required pre-merge status on the PR head'. Decision 4 notes that stealth mode has no host refs, so the plan already sees the host gap there. Fix: The guarantees table should name the fallback for each case: the post-merge attribution check fails a commit without a verified landing, and stealth mode checks locally before land pushes. Without this, the row overstates where the guarantee is enforced.

findings.summary: The 'Run' command (git status --porcelain) does not produce what the 'Observes' column describes. The evidence comes from reading the document.
findings.evidence: For example, criterion 3 runs git status but observes Grep hits for 'landing', 'squash' and 'parent'. Fix: List the Grep or Read of docs/design/records-history.md as the demonstration, and keep git status for criterion 9 only.

summary: The plan covers all seven required points and maps each to a criterion, and the files it names exist. I checked docs/decisions.md: its last entry is D111 at line 2580, so D112 is the right number. I checked athena.toml line 152: the six exempt shas the plan lists match it exactly, including 49c6ac1 and 64ecdc9, which the request did not name. The gate ordering is a sound answer to "no trailers": the content gate runs before the merge, and attribution is checked after it with a bounded pending state. The recommendation is argued against A4, A5 and D72. The demonstrations are content reads plus a git status/diff check. That fits a design-only job: criterion 9 would fail if a config or Rust file changed. I found no blocker or major problem. Two design points should be stated openly in the document rather than left implicit: what the parent-link reachability does to the "separate root", and who may write the checkpoint. A third smaller point is that the required pre-merge status depends on the host.
